meta.coord_system_note: coord_system selects the energy network's input frame on two-shower data only; it does not apply to this experiment.

estimator.name: median
estimator.label: Median |rel. err.|
estimator.definition: R = E_est / p per event; the median relative error median |R − 1| per momentum window, in percent, computed for a model series as median |E_est − p| / p: the Median rel. of Model Error vs. Incident Momentum, with its events, seed and interval.

interval.label: 95% percentile bootstrap of the median from N = 20 (B = 2,000, each replicate's median drawn exactly), the distribution-free order-statistic interval for 6 ≤ N < 20, none below: Model Error vs. Incident Momentum's own, seeded [42, frame, shower, bin, 2] with frame 0–2 the network frames (absolute, per-shower translated, local), 3 XGBoost and 4 the deposit, shower 0 for A and 1 for B.

weight.label: Fit weights 1/se², se = κ·ŷ with κ = SE / value the window's bootstrap relative SE (the SD, ddof = 1, of the replicates behind its interval), recomputed at the fitted value ŷ and iterated; the first fit takes the bootstrap SE itself. The Gaussian asymptotic law would understate these SEs.

literature.warning: Note: comparing Median |rel. err.| against a σ/E literature curve (for unbiased Gaussian errors, median|R − 1| = 0.6745·σ/E; use Robust σ (IQR) for a σ-scaled comparison).

calibration.label: Under Median |rel. err.| the deposit is c̃·E_dep, with c̃ = 1 / median(E_dep / p) over the shower's events of the selection with E_dep > 0: one constant per shower, the median analogue of the ratio of sums c = Σ p / Σ E_dep (c_sum), which is reported beside it. median |c·E_dep − p| / p depends on c; the robust and sample widths do not.

estimator.relation: For unbiased Gaussian errors median|R − 1| = 0.6745·σ/E, so a median relative error is quoted beside σ/E, never converted into it.

top.name: Energy (GeV) ⟶
top.rule: E = 1/x², an exact relabelling of the bottom axis; no data are plotted against it.

energy.rule: E = 1/x² of the 1/√E view's x = ⟨1/√p⟩: one exact bijection, so both views draw the same measurements.
notes: The E view's y range follows the windows alone, from zero: those with N ≥ 20 from 2 GeV, whiskers included; a window below 2 GeV never sets it. No fitted curve, band or extrapolation sets it: one that leaves the top is clipped there with a caret.
Fitted curves are drawn from 4 GeV, the lowest window edge any fit can use, to 80 GeV: solid over the windows each fit ran through, dashed beyond, where the curve extrapolates its form.

Each window is drawn at E = 1/x² with x = ⟨1/√p⟩, the abscissa the fits used, so a window on its fitted line in the 1/√E view sits on its fitted curve here; its ⟨p⟩, slightly larger (Jensen's inequality), is in its tooltip.

anchors.rule: Chosen on the whole table's bins, not the selection: the lowest bin from 5 GeV, the highest bin, and the bin between them nearest in log E to the geometric mean of their centres. A series whose anchor holds N < 20 takes its nearest window from 5 GeV in log E with N ≥ 20, named in substitutions; with fewer than two, windows of N ≥ 8 and the fit is provisional.

model.reason: No XGBoost models pair with this experiment: its source file name 'single_events.csv' does not name a species and seed (expected <species>_standalone_…_aggr_s<seed>_v<n>).

series.label: Shower · Calibrated deposit c·E_dep — linear-sum benchmark

windows.label: 3–4 GeV
windows.dof_note: N = 1: a single shower; no spread or uncertainty can be estimated.

affine.note: median rel. = a/√E + b: weighted least squares over 3 windows, weights 1/se², se = κ·ŷ with κ the window's bootstrap relative SE, recomputed at the fitted value (29 refits). χ²/ν = 0.178/1, p = 0.673. Provisional: fewer than two windows reach N = 20, so it runs through windows of N ≥ 8.

pinned.note: median rel. = a₀/√E, through the origin: weighted least squares over 3 windows, weights 1/se², se = κ·ŷ with κ the window's bootstrap relative SE, recomputed at the fitted value (2 refits). χ²/ν = 0.245/2, p = 0.885. Provisional: fewer than two windows reach N = 20, so it runs through windows of N ≥ 8.

quadrature.note: median rel. = √(a²/E + b²), fitted as (median rel.)² = A/E + B: weighted least squares over 3 windows, weights 1/se², se = κ·ŷ with κ the window's bootstrap relative SE, recomputed at the fitted value (13 refits). χ²/ν = 0.0642/1, p = 0.8. A ≤ 0, so a = √A is undefined; A is reported with its standard error. Provisional: fewer than two windows reach N = 20, so it runs through windows of N ≥ 8.

affine.note: median rel. = a/√E + b: weighted least squares over 4 windows, weights 1/se², se = κ·ŷ with κ the window's bootstrap relative SE, recomputed at the fitted value (26 refits). χ²/ν = 0.261/2, p = 0.878. Provisional: fewer than two windows reach N = 20, so it runs through windows of N ≥ 8.

pinned.note: median rel. = a₀/√E, through the origin: weighted least squares over 4 windows, weights 1/se², se = κ·ŷ with κ the window's bootstrap relative SE, recomputed at the fitted value (2 refits). χ²/ν = 1.03/3, p = 0.795. Provisional: fewer than two windows reach N = 20, so it runs through windows of N ≥ 8.

quadrature.note: median rel. = √(a²/E + b²), fitted as (median rel.)² = A/E + B: weighted least squares over 4 windows, weights 1/se², se = κ·ŷ with κ the window's bootstrap relative SE, recomputed at the fitted value (33 refits). χ²/ν = 0.23/2, p = 0.891. A ≤ 0, so a = √A is undefined; A is reported with its standard error. Provisional: fewer than two windows reach N = 20, so it runs through windows of N ≥ 8.

notes: The deposit E_dep is the producer's total_hit_energy and p its incoming_momentum, both read from the 59-column event aggregate: one shower per event, no hits.

Each window is the producer's integer momentum bin k, [k, k + 1) GeV, of the shower's own momentum. Per event R = E_est / p; the plotted value is the median relative error median |R − 1| in percent, for a model series median |E_est − p| / p: the Median rel. of Model Error vs. Incident Momentum, with its events, its seed and its interval, the 95% percentile bootstrap of the median from N = 20 (B = 2,000) and the distribution-free order-statistic interval below. Its abscissa is x = ⟨1/√p⟩ over the window's events. Dividing by p event by event removes the window's own momentum spread; unlike σ/E the median relative error keeps the estimator's bias, and it depends on the deposit's calibration.
For unbiased Gaussian errors median|R − 1| = 0.6745·σ/E, so a median relative error is quoted beside σ/E, never converted into it.
The detector series c·E_dep is a linear-sum benchmark, not a limit: a model that reads the shower's shape (leakage, compensation) can do better than a plain sum.
E on both axes is the incident momentum p as the producer writes it. For a massive species √(p² + m²) differs from p by at most m²/2p², 1.7% for a proton at 5 GeV/c.

The median rel. is reported from N = 2; a window is drawn with its whisker from N = 8 (its order-statistic interval exists from N = 6), and enters the fits and sets the y range from N = 20 and p ≥ 4 GeV.

Fits: a/√E + b and a₀/√E through the origin, by weighted least squares with weights 1/se², se = κ·ŷ with κ the window's bootstrap relative SE (the SD of the replicates behind its interval, over its value), taken at the fitted value ŷ and iterated (half steps once the refits oscillate); the first fit takes the bootstrap SE itself. χ², ν = n − p and its p-value. Where χ²/ν > 1 the standard errors and the 95% band are scaled by S = √(χ²/ν) (PDG), and the band then takes Student's t₀.₉₇₅,ν rather than 1.96, since S is estimated from the fit's own ν. The band is the 95% confidence band of the line, not the spread of the events. The quadrature form √(a²/E + b²) is fitted as (median rel.)² = A/E + B and tabled, not drawn. The three forms describe the median relative error: their parameters are not the stochastic and constant terms of a resolution.

A fit whose residuals average more than 5 of the windows' own standard errors (ν ≥ 1 and S = √(χ²/ν) > 5) has a form that does not describe its windows: it is drawn faded, as a provisional fit is, and said so in its tooltip, the fit table and the drawer. The size of the misfit decides, not the χ² p-value: a window of hundreds of events has so small a standard error that the test rejects a form for misfits no reader could see.

Anchors: the lowest bin from 5 GeV (below it the sampling fraction is still rising), the highest bin and the bin between them nearest in log E to the geometric mean of their centres, chosen on the whole table so they do not move with the selection. A series whose anchor window holds N < 20 takes its nearest window from 5 GeV in log E with N ≥ 20 instead; with fewer than two such windows its fit runs through windows of N ≥ 8 and is provisional. The other mode fits every window with N ≥ 20 from 4 GeV, the 4–5 GeV window included, below the anchors' floor.
The top axis is an exact relabelling of the bottom one, E = 1/x²: a deterministic unit conversion, and no data are plotted against it.

Shower: c̃ = 1 / median(E_dep / p) = 62.37 over the 286 events with E_dep > 0, fitted once over the selection, so the deposit's median response over them is 1; the ratio of sums c = Σ p / Σ E_dep = 105.8 beside it, which a low-side leakage tail would leave with a median response above 1.
No model series: No XGBoost models pair with this experiment: its source file name 'single_events.csv' does not name a species and seed (expected <species>_standalone_…_aggr_s<seed>_v<n>).
Off the axis: 3 windows below 4 GeV (29 events across the series) have x > 0.5; they are listed in off_axis with their median rel. and not drawn.

The y range follows the windows with N ≥ 20 (whiskers included) alone, from zero. No fit sets it: a fit summarises its windows and is not more evidence, so a fitted line or band that leaves the top is clipped there with a caret. 2 windows beyond it are clipped, not rescaled.
